title: Flash Flood Watch Continues — Athens County, 517 AM

fields.at: At 515 AM EDT, radar and automated rain gauges showed steady moderate rain continuing across southeast Ohio. Around 2 inches of rain fell overnight, and soils and small streams are already running high. An additional 2 to 3 inches is expected through noon, with the heaviest rates between 7 AM and 10 AM. Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible.
fields.hazard: Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall.
fields.impact: Excessive runoff may cause flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas and low-lying spots.
actions: You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
A Flash Flood Watch means that conditions may develop that lead to flash flooding. Flash flooding is a very dangerous situation. Small creeks draining hilly terrain can rise several feet in an hour.

instructorNote: Hand this to the IC and Facilities together with the Facilities dashboard screenshot for the Mill Street gauge (05:00 3.9 ft, 05:15 4.0 ft, 05:30 4.2 ft, RISING; action stage 5.0 ft, flood stage 7.0 ft). Watch for the IC to confirm Level 3, log the time, the 517 AM watch and the 4.2 ft reading as the basis (EOP Annex F section 4), and set the 5.0 ft trigger for opening the EOC in room 108 in advance; Facilities should assign a gauge watcher and plan on 1.5 ft per hour, which puts 5.0 ft about 30–40 minutes away (Annex F section 2).
